en.prompt: At Monterey Bay Aquarium, a five-year-old asks why caregivers groomed rescued sea otter pup 696. In a classroom demonstration invented for this question, two equally warm jars have identical model coats in the same cold bath. With air trapped in the fluffy coat, one jar cools 4 degrees in 20 minutes. With the coat wet and flat, the other cools 3 degrees in 10 minutes. A child says the fluffy jar lost warmth faster because four is more than three. Neither jar was tested for floating. Real sea otters lack thick blubber; grooming traps air in their fur, which helps them stay warm and float. Answer the child in at most five short sentences: use a fair comparison, explain whether air makes heat, and say what the jars can and cannot show about floating. Write the answer in English.
checks: Uses an equal-time comparison to explain the apparent reversal (2 degrees versus 3 per 10 minutes, or equivalent rates) and identifies the fluffy coat as slower to cool on average.
Connects grooming to trapped air keeping warmth from leaving as fast, without claiming that air creates heat or substituting an invented biological mechanism.
In at most five short child-facing sentences, separates the jars’ untested floating behavior from the fact that trapped air also helps real otters float.
